payload.name: Preserve participation action in community memories
payload.description: When extracting a user statement about joining or participating in a community/forum and discussing a topic, preserve the concrete activity verb (posting, commenting, discussing, writing) instead of only membership or a generic talk.
content: During extraction, if a user mentions joining or being active in a community/forum and talking about a topic, record the concrete participatory action they performed (e.g., posting, commenting, discussing, writing) as part of the memory content, not just the membership or a generic 'had a discussion'.

When the statement indicates a recurring or ongoing activity, phrase the memory as a durable activity (subject performs action on topic in that channel) so later questions about the user's writing or participation can be answered from the memory.

solves: When users describe joining or participating in an online community and talking about a topic, extraction may record only the membership or a generic discussion and drop the concrete writing/commenting/posting activity. This rule preserves the participatory action so future questions about the user's activities are answerable. It applies during candidate extraction from statements with an explicit participatory action, not to ordinary conversational messages without one.
